llm.model_note: 'jev-latest' is an alias; the provider echoes the exact version that ran (recorded per call as model_returned)
llm.temperature_note: not applicable: Jev returns typed decisions and exposes no sampling parameter or seed

production_llm_path.statement: The production chat has a Jev analytics path (question -> typed decisions + deterministic extraction -> validated structured request -> deterministic query engine -> verified result -> templated answer); it needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY. Without one the legacy router answers.

system_labels.decisiongpt: DecisionGPT production chat, Jev analytics path (TypeSafe AI Jev returns typed decisions about the question; deterministic code extracts periods/products/limits -> validated structured request -> deterministic query engine -> verified result -> templated answer); any answer served by the legacy fixed-intent router is flagged path=legacy_router and is NOT an AI answer - Target B (Jev)
system_labels.llm_code_baseline: Reference tool-use system: needs a text/code-generating model and CANNOT run on Jev (typed decisions only); retained for the record (NOT a simpler baseline, NOT DecisionGPT)

view.rules: 1) keep lines whose quantity is a whole number > 0 (sales.quantity is an integer column); 2) keep lines whose recomputed amount (qty*rate) agrees with a printed amount column; 3) merge lines that share (date, product, unit price) by summing quantity (the production upload validator rejects duplicate rows; merging preserves total sales and total units exactly; when a merged group mixed GST slabs, the slab with the largest revenue in the group is kept). Consequence: 'one row' no longer means 'one bill line', so no task asks about individual sale entries.

ground_truth_isolation.guard: whitelist check of every interpreter request + ground-truth fragment scan; a violating request is never sent and aborts the run

model_identity.seed_note: Jev has no sampling parameter or seed; repeats are independent requests
model_identity.retry_policy: none: exactly one HTTP attempt per call (a failed or ambiguous call is never re-sent, so it cannot spend more credits); per-request timeout from JEV_TIMEOUT_SECONDS; attempt counts are recorded per call
